Romania shot down a drone on Sunday, according to officials, marking the third time in as many days NATO aircraft have shot down uncrewed aerial vehicles. A Romanian F-16 fighter jet intercepted the drone at 10:13 a.m. local time close to the country's border with southwestern Ukraine, said Romanian President Nicușor Dan. Bucharest has frequently reported drone incursions from Ukraine when Russia bombards Ukrainian ports close to the Danube River, which splits Romanian soil from Ukraine. Read More on World Romania shares roughly 400 miles of land border with Ukraine. ... Drones intruding into NATO airspace have not been treated as attacks on the alliance so far, meaning they have not triggered discussions over a collective response from all 32 members. But the persistent incidents have pushed the alliance's members along Europe's eastern edge to invest in anti-drone defenses. Romania's defense ministry said on Sunday the drone was shot down "safely" little over seven miles northeast of the port of Sulina, within Romania's territorial waters. Romanian authorities didn't confirm whether the drone intercepted on Sunday was Russian-made but Dan said it was "intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romania's airspace, which is, at the same time, NATO airspace and European Union airspace." On Saturday, Romanian officials said a drone had been taken out in an unpopulated area close to the border with Ukraine after it was picked up by radar systems at 8:22 a.m. local time. This incident came a day after NATO said two Romanian F-16s and two Italian Eurofighter jets were scrambled under the alliance's command on Friday to intercept a drone that had approached Romania's airspace. Romanian investigators later said the drone was Russian-made. Debris from the drone and the intercept missile landed close to two towns northeast of Bucharest, the Romanian defense ministry said. No casualties or injuries were reported. The governor of Ukraine's southwestern Odesa region, which sits next to Romania, issued several air raid alerts for the areas along the border in the early hours of Sunday. Russia's defense ministry said on Sunday it had attacked the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk, southwest of the city of Odesa, targeting fuel tanks used by the Ukrainian military. Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Romania’s Energy Ministry has restated the government's plea for household consumers, companies and public institutions to reduce electricity consumption between 7 PM and 11 PM until the end of August amid the ongoing energy crisis. The plea comes as Romania is experiencing an energy crisis generated mainly by the severe drought and the sharp reduction in the flow of the Danube, which has recorded the lowest level in approximately the last 40 years, lowering the energy generation of Nuclearelectrica (BVB: SNN) and Hidroelectrica (BVB: H20). The drought is set to continue, with no short-term improvement, according to the most recent forecasts. As supply problems persist, demand must be lowered, according to the government. As a result, a nationwide state of alert was established in Romania for 30 days starting on July 31. Since then, several city halls and public institutions have taken measures to reduce electricity consumption, and Romania’s biggest energy consumers, the Ford and Dacia factories, agreed to end production until August 19. In this context, limiting energy consumption in the evening is meant to protect the energy supply and reduce the risk of restrictive measures being introduced. The ministry gave assurances that all responsible institutions are acting in a coordinated manner to ensure the proper supply of electricity. To help coordinate voluntary reductions in energy consumption, the ministry published recommendations for all categories of consumers. Household consumers Household consumers are encouraged to reduce the simultaneous use of equipment with high electricity consumption between 7 PM and 11 PM and to reschedule these activities between 11 AM and 5 PM, when electricity production from photovoltaic sources is higher. Washing machines, dishwashers, clothes dryers, electric vehicle chargers, and electric boilers are some of the energy-intensive household equipment. Importantly, the ministry did not ask Romanians to turn off devices necessary for protecting health, maintaining a tolerable temperature in homes, or operating medical equipment. Large industrial consumers Large industrial consumers, which use more than 50,000 MWh annually, are encouraged to analyze reducing consumption during evenings, where the specifics of the technological process and safety requirements allow it. The measures may include rescheduling flexible processes, using their own production or storage capacities, and avoiding the start-up of high-power equipment during peak hours. At the same time, companies should send emails to consumatori@energie.gov.ro and office@transelectrica.ro , as well as to the electricity supplier with which they have concluded the supply contract, specifying the measures that can be applied, the period and time of their application, the estimated reduction in consumption, and the name, position, and contact details of the person designated for coordination. Consumption reduction must not affect the security of installations, employee protection, continuity of critical processes or environmental protection obligations. Smaller non-household consumers Smaller non-household energy consumers were also encouraged to limit consumption during evening hours. Measures that may be considered include reducing non-essential lighting, turning off unused equipment, avoiding the charging of electric vehicles during peak hours and rescheduling activities with high consumption. Public institutions Public institutions, in turn, were asked to reduce their consumption too. To do so, institutions may consider turning off architectural and decorative lighting; reducing lighting in unused spaces; turning off equipment that is not necessary after working hours; limiting air conditioning in unoccupied spaces; and rescheduling administrative activities with high consumption. These recommendations do not apply to hospitals, emergency services, intervention units, water supply systems, critical infrastructure or other essential public services. Finally, the Ministry asked prosumers who have batteries to charge their storage systems between 11 AM and 5 PM, especially from their own production, and to use the stored energy between 7 PM and 11 PM. In this way, prosumers can reduce their consumption from the grid exactly during the period when the National Energy System is under the greatest pressure. radu@romania-insider.com (Photo source: bubbersbb|Dreamstime.com ) Read next 06 August 2026 Energy Energy demand spikes in Romania despite government's plea to limit consumption Normal Energy Romanian authorities launch new appeal to limit electricity consumption amid drought 06 August 2026 Radu Dumitrescu Like this article?
